rescueTop10.event: Accession of Cyrus II in Anshan
rescueTop10.significance: Cyrus becomes tributary King of Anshan in Persis under Median overlord Astyages.

rescueTop10.event: Overthrow of Astyages & Capture of Ecbatana
rescueTop10.significance: Astyages’ Median army mutinies (Nabonidus Chronicle); Cyrus spares Astyages and absorbs Media.

rescueTop10.event: Conquest of Lydia & Fall of Sardis
rescueTop10.significance: After Delphi’s oracle and Pteria, Cyrus marches in winter, uses camels at Thymbra, takes Sardis, and subdues Ionia.
After Battle of Opis, Babylon falls; Cyrus restores Marduk’s cult and permits exiled peoples including Jews to return.
Cyrus builds royal garden-palace and tomb at Pasargadae before dying on campaign against the Massagetae.
Defeats Psammetichus III at Pelusium and takes Memphis; Udjahorresnet’s inscription counters Herodotus’ Apis bull slander.

rescueTop10.event: Bardiya/Gaumata Crisis & Accession of Darius I
rescueTop10.significance: Cambyses dies; Darius overthrows Bardiya/Gaumata, crushes 9 revolts, and carves the Bisitun Inscription.
Darius reorganises 20 satrapies, gold Darics, Susa/Persepolis, crushes the Ionian Revolt (499–493 BC), and loses Marathon (490 BC).

rescueTop10.event: Xerxes I’s Invasion: Thermopylae, Sack of Athens & Salamis
rescueTop10.significance: Bridges Hellespont, forces Thermopylae, burns Athenian Acropolis, but Greek triremes win at Salamis.

rescueTop10.event: Plataea, Mycale, Eurymedon & Persepolis Gate of All Nations
rescueTop10.significance: Mardonius falls at Plataea (479 BC); Xerxes consolidates empire and monumentalises Persepolis until 465 BC.

anchors.title: The conquest of Babylon
anchors.recallPrompt: What key historical facts and ancient evidence must you recall for: "The conquest of Babylon"?
facts: Nabonidus alienated Marduk’s Esagila priests by promoting the moon-god Sin and staying 10 years at Tayma (halting the Akitu festival).
Autumn 539 BC: Cyrus defeated Nabonidus at Opis on the Tigris; Sippar yielded (10 Oct) and Ugbaru entered Babylon without battle (12 Oct), contrasted with Herodotus 1.191’s Euphrates diversion tale.

anchors.title: Cyrus' attitude towards conquered peoples and his liberation of the Jews
anchors.recallPrompt: What key historical facts and ancient evidence must you recall for: "Cyrus' attitude towards conquered peoples and his liberation of the Jews"?
facts: Cyrus entered Babylon (29 Oct 539 BC), guarded Esagila, and issued the Akkadian Cyrus Cylinder restoring Mesopotamian cult statues and deportees.
538 BC Edict of Restoration (Ezra 1 & 6; Isaiah 45:1): freed Jewish exiles to rebuild Yahweh’s Temple in Jerusalem with Nebuchadnezzar’s returned vessels.

subTopics.title: 1.3 Pasargadae and the Death of Cyrus

anchors.title: The construction of Pasargadae
anchors.recallPrompt: What key historical facts and ancient evidence must you recall for: "The construction of Pasargadae"?
facts: Built in Persis from c. 546 BC using Lydian-Ionian ashlar masons (iron dovetail clamps) alongside Babylonian and Elamite sculptors across Palace S and Palace P.
Gate R’s four-winged guardian (Egyptian hemhem crown + Assyrian wings + Elamite robe), stone-irrigated four-part pairidaeza garden, and six-stepped limestone Tomb of Cyrus.

anchors.title: The circumstances of Cyrus' death
anchors.recallPrompt: What key historical facts and ancient evidence must you recall for: "The circumstances of Cyrus' death"?
facts: 530 BC: Herodotus 1.214 claims Queen Tomyris of the Massagetae killed Cyrus and dipped his head in blood after Spargapises’ death, admitting rival stories existed.
Ctesias attributed his death to a wound fighting the Derbices, Xenophon gave a peaceful deathbed, and Arrian 6.29 confirms his intact body lay in a golden coffin at Pasargadae.
